source.title: RoboMME: Benchmarking and Understanding Memory for Robotic Generalist Policies
source.policy: The prompt specifications are concise summaries of Appendix E only; they contain no episode-specific labels, oracle plans, or hidden environment state.

tasks.BinFill: The robot must place the exact requested number of red, green, and blue cubes into the bin, then press the button to stop. In the Static setting, all cubes are present from the beginning. In the Streaming setting, cubes appear incrementally in a random order. Placing more than the requested number of any color causes immediate failure.
tasks.PickXtimes: The robot must pick up the specified cube and place it on the target exactly the number of times requested by the instruction, then press the button to stop. A valid pick-and-place repetition requires lifting the cube above the required height and lowering it onto the target. Picking the wrong cube, pressing the button too early, or performing more repetitions than requested causes failure.
tasks.SwingXtimes: The robot must pick up the specified cube, move it to the right-side target, and then move it to the left-side target. One right-to-left traversal counts as one complete cycle. Target highlighting changes from gray to red when a valid target is reached. The robot must complete the requested number of cycles, put down the cube, and press the button to stop. Extra target visits cause failure.
tasks.StopCube: A cube continuously moves back and forth along a straight path. The robot must press the button so that the cube stops while overlapping the target on the requested visit. The robot can first position the end effector above the button and remain still while waiting for the correct timing. The motion delay between hovering and physically pressing the button must be considered. Stopping the cube on an earlier or later visit causes failure.
tasks.VideoUnmask: The video shows colored cubes being hidden under multiple containers while the robot remains stationary. Some containers may be empty. During execution, the robot must pick up the container hiding each cube color requested by the instruction. If multiple containers are requested, they must be picked up in the specified order. Picking up an incorrect container causes immediate failure.
tasks.ButtonUnmask: The robot must first press the button. During the button-press phase, containers are placed over the colored cubes, and some containers may be empty. After observing this process, the robot must pick up the container or containers hiding the requested cube colors. When multiple containers are required, the robot must release the first container before picking up the next one. Picking up a container before completing the button phase or picking up an incorrect container causes failure.
tasks.VideoUnmaskSwap: The video shows colored cubes being hidden under containers, followed by one or more container swaps while the robot remains stationary. The robot must track the identity of each container through the swaps. During execution, it must pick up the container or containers hiding the requested cube colors, in the specified order. Picking up an incorrect container causes immediate failure.
tasks.ButtonUnmaskSwap: The robot must first press both buttons on the table. During the button-press phase, containers enclose the colored cubes and some containers swap positions. After completing both button presses, the robot must pick up the container or containers hiding the requested cube colors, in the specified order. Picking up a container before the button phase is complete or picking up an incorrect container causes failure.
tasks.PickHighlight: The robot must first press the button. During the press, the cubes that must be picked are briefly indicated by white visual highlights for a limited number of timesteps. The robot must remember all highlighted cubes after the cues disappear and pick up each correct cube. Attempting a pick before pressing the button or picking up an unhighlighted cube causes failure. If the episode instruction requests a final button press to stop, the robot must perform it after the required pickups.
tasks.VideoRepick: The video shows the robot picking up and placing one specific cube instance. Afterward, the cubes may swap positions while the robot remains still. During execution, the robot must locate the same demonstrated cube instance and repeat the pick-and-place action exactly the number of times specified by the instruction, then press the button to stop. Picking the wrong cube, pressing the button too early, or performing too many repetitions causes failure.
tasks.VideoPlaceButton: The video shows a cube being placed on multiple targets, with a button press interleaved between placement events. The instruction identifies the required target using a temporal relation, such as immediately before or immediately after the button press. In the Hard setting, two targets may swap positions after the demonstrated sequence. During execution, the robot must pick up the specified cube and place it on the correct target. Picking the wrong cube or placing it on the wrong target causes immediate failure.
tasks.VideoPlaceOrder: The video shows a cube being placed on multiple targets in a specific temporal order, with button presses between placements. The instruction identifies the required target by its ordinal position in the demonstrated sequence, such as the third target visited. In the Hard setting, two targets may swap positions after the sequence. During execution, the robot must pick up the specified cube and place it on the requested target. Picking the wrong cube or using the wrong target causes immediate failure.
tasks.MoveCube: The demonstration moves a cube to a target using exactly one of three manipulation methods: (1) Hooking: pick up a peg tool and use it to hook or move the cube to the target; (2) Pushing: keep the gripper closed and use the closed gripper to push the cube across the table to the target; or (3) Pick-and-place: directly grasp the cube, lift it, and place it on the target. After the demonstration, the cube and target are reset to new random positions. During execution, the robot must reproduce the demonstrated manipulation method while adapting to the new configuration. Using a different method causes immediate failure.
tasks.InsertPeg: The video demonstrates three task-defining attributes: which peg is selected, which end of that peg is grasped (head or tail), and which side of the box is used for insertion (left or right). After the demonstration, all pegs return to their original positions and orientations without randomization. During execution, the robot must select the same peg, grasp the same end, and insert it into the same side of the box. Selecting the wrong peg, grasping the wrong end, or using the wrong insertion side causes immediate failure.
tasks.PatternLock: The video shows a stick attached to the robot tracing a continuous pattern over a grid of targets. The demonstration defines an ordered sequence of targets. During execution, the robot must visit the same targets in the same order while maintaining a continuous trajectory. A gray target turns red when the stick makes a valid visit, and the stick-tip trajectory is rendered in real time. Skipping a target or deviating from the demonstrated order causes failure.
tasks.RouteStick: The video shows a stick attached to the robot navigating among fixed vertical obstacles while visiting a sequence of targets. The demonstration implicitly specifies both the target order and whether each obstacle is circled clockwise or counterclockwise. During execution, the robot must visit the same targets in the same order, match the demonstrated circling direction around each obstacle, and maintain one continuous trajectory. Targets turn red when visited, and the stick-tip trajectory is rendered in real time. Hard cases may include backtracking. Deviating from the demonstrated order causes failure.
